record.paper_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
record.original_question: What are the vulnerabilities, attack models, and effective countermeasures for magnetic-induction-based underwater wireless communication networks, including how confidentiality, authentication, integrity, and availability can be achieved in systems whose predictable channel response may expose them to eavesdropping and spoofing and whose nearby malicious coils may exploit mutual induction?

evidence.quote: To the best of our knowledge, there is no work reported on the vulnerabilities, attacks and countermeasures on MI based underwater WCNs.
This implies that all the four properties (i.e., confidentiality, authentication, integrity and availability) are yet to be studied for MI based underwater WCN.

However, we believe that the predictable channel response of such networks makes it vulnerable to some attacks, e.g., eavesdropping and spoofing. Moreover, a malicious coil present in the closed vicinity of the legitimate coil may get benefit from mutual induction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an underwater wireless communication network in which each node is equipped with a coil antenna and information is transferred between nodes via magnetic induction (MI): a transmitting coil drives a time-varying current that, by mutual inductance, induces a voltage in a receiving coil. Assume the network operates in a conducting aqueous medium where the MI channel response between two coils is essentially deterministic once their geometry (separation, orientation, coil parameters) and the medium's permeability and conductivity are fixed, so that the channel is highly predictable. Adversaries may (i) passively eavesdrop on legitimate transmissions, (ii) spoof legitimate nodes by exploiting the predictable channel, and (iii) place malicious coils in close proximity to legitimate coils to couple to them via mutual induction.

Develop a complete security framework for such an MI-based underwater wireless communication network. Specifically:

1. Formulate a precise threat model that enumerates the vulnerabilities of MI underwater links, including those arising from channel predictability and from mutual-induction coupling with nearby unauthorized coils.

2. Specify attack models (eavesdropping, spoofing, impersonation, denial-of-service via induced interference, and mutual-induction-based information leakage) together with quantitative metrics for their success probability as a function of coil geometry, medium parameters, and noise.

3. Design and rigorously justify countermeasures that simultaneously guarantee
   (a) confidentiality of transmitted messages,
   (b) authentication of legitimate transmitters and receivers,
   (c) integrity of the exchanged data, and
   (d) availability of the communication service,
in the presence of the above adversaries, and prove (or otherwise establish) the security guarantees achieved.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that security of magnetic-induction-based underwater wireless communication networks remains an underexplored research direction. While MI underwater channel modeling and physical-layer studies have advanced, surveys and recent works continue to flag confidentiality, authentication, integrity, and availability for MI underwater WCNs as open problems with no comprehensive solution reported.

status_evidence.title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys identify vulnerabilities, attacks and countermeasures for MI-based underwater wireless communication networks as an open research area, with all four security properties yet to be studied.
status_evidence.claim: The security of MI-based underwater WCNs (confidentiality, authentication, integrity, availability) is unresolved in the literature.
